AgentStatus.description:
Represents the status of an agent, including assignment details, activity state, and other information.
This class is also used for requesting AgentStatus, in which case only info_type and status_type are required fields.

Attributes:
    team_id (Optional[str]): ID of the team this agent belongs to. Defaults to 'NO_TEAM'.
    named_agent_type (Optional[str]): Named type of the agent. Will be used during instantiation requests to look up and set agent's parameters (e.g. role, backstory, tools). Not unique - e.g: CodeWritingAgent
    self_id (Optional[str]): ID of current agent. This is synonymous with the ID of the queue on which this agent is listening.
    is_paused (Optional[bool]): Indicates whether the processing is paused.
    is_executing (Optional[bool]): Indicates whether the agent's execution slot is currently occupied.
    has_execution_capacity (Optional[bool]): Indicates whether the agent can immediately start executing another top-level task.
    is_busy (Optional[bool]): Deprecated alias for is_executing.
    name (Optional[str]): Unique (typically randomly generated) name of the agent to help LLMs remember it.
    tools (Optional[List[str]]): List of tools at this agent's disposal. Defaults to an empty list.
    available_skills (Optional[List[str]]): Semantic names of skills this agent can activate. Defaults to an empty list.
    is_exiting (Optional[bool]): Indicates whether the agent is exiting and this is its last status update. Defaults to False.
    is_team_lead (Optional[bool]): Indicates whether this agent is team leader. Defaults to False.
    top_level_queue_depth (Optional[int]): Runnable queued top-level tasks waiting to execute.
    waiting_top_level_task_count (Optional[int]): Top-level tasks blocked in WAITING.
    deferred_message_count (Optional[int]): Inbound messages deferred while execution capacity was unavailable.
    diagnostic (Optional[dict]): Optional diagnostic information like available memory, queue metrics, number of messages in conversation, uptime, current problem being worked etc. Defaults to None.
    agent_pubkey (Optional[str]): Optional agent's public key for secure communication.
    agent_role (Optional[str]): Agent's self-reported role.
    info_type (ControlType): Specifies the type of status information requested or provided (e.g., basic, full). Defaults to ControlType.STATUS_REQUEST_BASIC.
    status_type (MessageMetaType): Indicates whether this is a request for status or a response to a request with own status.

MessageHeader.description:
Contains standard routing and identification metadata for a message.

Attributes:
    from_agent_id (Optional[str]):
        Optional identifier of the agent originating the message. Useful for tracking message origin
        and facilitating direct responses. Defaults to None if the message isn't directly associated with an agent.

    to_routing_path (Optional[Union[str, RoutingType]]):
        Optional identifier of the agent intended to receive the message, or a special routing type.
        Used for routing messages to specific agents or groups within the system.
        Special routing types include: '++<all>++', '++<self>++', '++<null>++'.
        Defaults to None if the message is not targeted at a specific agent.

    response_routing_key (Optional[Union[str, RoutingType]]):
        Optional routing key (e.g., queue name) or a special routing type where a response to this message should be sent.
        Defaults to None if no specific response routing is required.

    timestamp (str):
        Timestamp indicating when the message was created, automatically generated using the
        ISO 8601 format. Provides a standardized time reference for all messages.

    message_id (str):
        Unique identifier for the message, automatically generated with a semantic prefix
        and a 12-character lowercase hexadecimal suffix. Ensures message
        uniqueness and facilitates tracking.

    agent_signature (Optional[str]):
        Optional signature of the agent's private key applied to the message_id of this message (for security).

PersonStandingCommandV1.description:
Gateway-to-manager: a person's standing changed; bring the manager's records in line.

Sent by the gateway after ``/user disable``, ``/user remove``,
``/user enable``, adding someone back and ``/user restore``. The manager
acts on the person's standing in the gateway's people copy
(``access_control.people_directory``), not on ``standing`` here, so a late
or repeated command never acts on an old standing; ``standing`` is what
the gateway expects, and a mismatch is logged. Only the gateway may send
it: the manager requires the gateway-signed task context of an active
administrator (``custom_agents.person_departure_runtime``), and agents
cannot send manager control messages at all. Like every gateway command,
it names the acting person only through that signed context
(``custom_agents.manager_control_runtime.verified_command_person``).

SchedulePermitV1.description:
The manager's signed statement that one schedule's runs work for one person.

The scheduler signs it once per schedule and renews it before it expires
(``custom_agents.schedule_permits``), so a worker that holds no key can
start the schedule's runs without asking the manager each time. It names
no roles: whoever checks a run reads the person's current roles and
standing, and the schedule row's current owner (``access_control.task_identity``).
``person_id`` None is system work for no person, only for the runtime's
maintenance schedule of a built-in system agent. ``record_kind`` and the
signature's own domain keep a permit from ever passing as a task context.

they tie the run's tasks together and date the run, and grant nothing.

ScheduledMessage.description:
A scheduled message that fires on this agent at a specified time, once or on a recurring basis.

Schedules are persisted through the configured schedule repository backend
so they survive agent restarts.
When a schedule fires, its embedded Task payload is processed by the agent's LLM.

Scheduling modes (mutually exclusive):
    - interval_ms: Fixed-interval repeat in milliseconds.
    - cron_expression: Cron string (e.g. "*/5 * * * *") for complex schedules,
      read in ``cron_timezone`` ("0 9 * * *" is 9:00 in that zone, across
      daylight saving changes).

Attributes:
    schedule_id (str): Unique identifier for this schedule.
    payload (Task): The Task to execute when the schedule fires.
    interval_ms (Optional[int]): Fixed-interval repeat in milliseconds.
    cron_expression (Optional[str]): Cron expression for complex scheduling.
    repeat_count (Optional[int]): Number of times to fire. None = infinite, 1 = once.
    next_fire_at (Optional[str]): ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of next scheduled fire.
    created_at (str): ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when this schedule was created.
    enabled (bool): Whether this schedule is active. Can be paused without deleting.

Task.description:
Represents a task request or a response containing subtask results/answers.

Attributes:
    task_id (str): Unique identifier for the task. Defaults to `task_id_` plus a 12-character lowercase hexadecimal suffix. For a task object carrying a response, the task_id must match the original task_id of the received task it is a response to.
    parent_task_id (Optional[str]): Id of the parent task (if this is a subtask request). Every subtask request and response must have a parent_task_id. Defaults to None.
    task_state (List[Tuple[ProgressState, str]]): Task status list, where each tuple contains the state and a timestamp string. Defaults to an empty list.
    task_queries (Optional[List["TaskQuery"]]): List of task queries (conversations about this task), generated by agents to clarify intent or ask questions. Defaults to an empty list.
    task_type (MessageMetaType): Indicates whether this object represents a request for a task to be performed or a response to a previous task (i.e., a subtask response or final answer).
    problem_statement (Optional[str]): Clearly defined problem statement and execution instructions for the agent (required for requests, optional for responses).
    errors (Optional[List[str]]): List of errors generated during task execution. Defaults to None.
    answers (Union[List[Task, str, None]]): Either a (potentially partial) list of subtask responses to the parent task or a single string holding an answer to a subtask or the final answer to the original task request. Defaults to None.

answer.description: The answer to the task. Can be a simple string or a structured TaskAnswer object containing tools used. TaskAnswer objects are preferred.
answer.title: Answer

attachments.description: User-provided attachment references. Binary bytes are stored outside the task payload.

ToolSetupRequestV1.description:
Trusted code asks the person to set up one tool so TeamLead's task can use it.

Sent only by ``set_up_tools`` (``custom_agents.tool_setup_run_runtime``),
never written by a model. The gateway opens the matching secure broker
page in the chat of the person the task works for: their own sign-in page
(``sign_in``), the labeled account link form (``account_link``;
``owner="team"`` needs a team administrator), or the page that stores the
team's sign-in app (``team_sign_in_app``; administrators only). For an
``external_step`` it shows the catalog's words for that step (named by
``step_id``; ``owner="team"`` when only an administrator can do it) and
waits until the person marks it done on the workflow page. The task waits
for one ``ToolSetupResultV1``. Setting a tool up never grants access to
it: access comes from grants.

owner.description: Whose account or app: the team's or the person's own.
owner.title: Owner

parent_task_id.description: Task waiting for the setup result.
parent_task_id.title: Parent Task Id

reason.description: One plain sentence the person reads: why the task needs this.
reason.title: Reason

step_id.description: For an external_step: the step id in the tool's catalog setup data.
step_id.title: Step Id

tool_id.description: Catalog tool id, for example cli:github or http:portainer.
tool_id.title: Tool Id

ToolSetupRequestV1.title: ToolSetupRequestV1

ToolSetupResultV1.description:
How one setup page ended, sent to the task waiting for it; no secrets.

``message`` is a plain sentence TeamLead may relay; ``account_label`` is
the account the person signed in with when the broker knows it (for
example ``exampleuser``). ``needs_administrator`` says only a team
administrator can do this step. ``attempt`` counts the pages of this kind
the task offered for the tool (at most ``TOOL_SETUP_OFFER_LIMIT``).
ToolSetupResultV1.title: ToolSetupResultV1

User-visible notification emitted by an agent through the gateway.

This is intentionally separate from Task responses: tasks can originate from
GitHub, schedules, webhooks, or other automations while user communication
still follows the gateway-owned preferred contact profile.
